II. one was the wife or husband of a lineal ascendant or descendant of the other, including relationship by half blood or full blood.
III. one was the wife of the brother or of the father’s or mother’s brother or of the grandfather’s or grandmother’s brother of the other.
IV. the two are brother and sister, uncle and niece, aunt and nephew, or children of two brothers and sisters. Select the correct answer.
explanation: Section 3(g) of the Hindu Marriage Act defines the degrees of prohibited relationship. Each of statements I to IV reads like part of that definition, so all four look correct.

stem: The Central Consumer Protection Council, as provided under Section 3(2) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, shall consist of:

options.text: A Chairperson and ten other members, or a Chairperson and such other members as may be prescribed
A Chairperson and five other members
A Chairperson and such other members as may be prescribed
A Chairperson and ten other members

stem: Under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, which of the following orders is not appealable?

options.text: Refusing to refer parties to arbitration under Section 8
Refusing to appoint arbitrator under Section 11
Refusing to grant any measure under Section 9
Refusing to grant an interim measure under Section 17

explanation: Section 37 allows an appeal against an order refusing interim measures under Section 17, so that is appealable. An order refusing to appoint an arbitrator under Section 11 is not listed, and the Supreme Court has held that no appeal lies against it.

stem:
As per Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for Res Judicata to be applicable on a subsequent suit, the former suit must satisfy the following conditions:
I. has been finally decided.
II. can only be instituted prior to the subsequent suit.
III. relates to the same matter directly and substantially in issue in the subsequent suit.
IV. is between the same parties, or between parties under whom they or any of them claim. Select the correct answer.
explanation: Res judicata requires that the former suit has been finally decided, that the matter was directly and substantially in issue in both, and that the parties are the same or claim under the same persons. It does not require that the former suit was instituted earlier, only decided earlier, so statement II is wrong.

stem: As per the Indian Contract Act, 1872, an acceptance must be absolute and unqualified. What is the legal effect if an offeree’s response introduces a new term?

options.text: It becomes a valid acceptance, and the new term is incorporated as a mere suggestion.
It operates as a valid acceptance if the new term is not a material alteration.
It constitutes a counter-proposal, thereby rejecting the original proposal.
It suspends the original proposal until the new term is accepted or rejected by the proposer.

explanation: An acceptance must be absolute and unqualified. A response that adds a new term is not an acceptance; it is a counter-proposal, which rejects the original proposal.

stem: Which of the following is incorrect with respect to diary of proceedings in investigation as per the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973?

options.text: The statements of witnesses recorded during investigation shall be inserted in the diary.
The diary shall be duly paginated.
The diary may be used as evidence.
Can be used by the police officers to refresh memory.

explanation: The police case diary is for the court and the police to use in the inquiry or trial, not as evidence in the case. A statement that it may be used as evidence is therefore the incorrect one.

stem: Which of the following doctrine has been applied to resolve the conflict between Article 25(2)(b) and 26(b) of the Constitution of India?
explanation: When two provisions both protect religious interests, the court reads them together so that each has effect where possible. This is the doctrine of harmonious construction; the other doctrines listed do not resolve conflicts between two constitutional provisions.

stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect as per The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?

options.text: A contracts, in writing, with B, for the delivery of indigo upon certain terms. The contract mentions the fact that B had paid A the price of other indigo contracted for, verbally, on another occasion. Oral evidence is offered that no payment was made for the other indigo. The evidence is admissible.

B agrees absolutely in writing to pay B one thousand rupees on 1st March, 2023. The fact that, at the same time, an oral agreement was made that the money should not be paid till 31st March, 2023, can be proved.
A enters into a written contract with B to work certain mines, the property of B, upon certain terms. A was induced to do so by a misrepresentation of B as to their value. This fact may be proved.

A orders goods from B by a letter in which nothing is said as to the time of payment, and accepts the goods on delivery. B sues A for the price. A may show that the goods were supplied on credit for a term still unexpired.

explanation: The provision bars oral evidence that contradicts or varies the terms of a written contract. An oral agreement made at the same time that the money would not be paid until later, contradicting an absolute written promise, cannot be proved. The statement saying it can be proved is therefore the incorrect one.

stem:
Where the decree is for payment of money, execution by detention in prison shall not be ordered unless the Court is satisfied that:
I. the judgment-debtor is likely to abscond or leave jurisdiction.
II. the judgment-debtor has dishonestly transferred property before the suit.
III. the decree is for a sum for which the judgment-debtor was in a fiduciary capacity to account.
IV. the judgment-debtor has or had the means to pay substantial amount but neglected to pay. Select the correct answer.
explanation: Detention of a judgment-debtor on a money decree is allowed only on the grounds in the proviso to section 51: likely to abscond, dishonest transfer of property after the suit began, fiduciary liability, or means to pay but refusal. Statement II says "before the suit", so it does not match.

stem: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India hold that the rule of nemo judex in causa sua is subject to the doctrine of necessity?

options.text: Sahni Silk Mills (P) Ltd. v. Employees’ State Insurance Corporation, (1994) 5 SCC 346
In Re: Delhi Laws Act, AIR 1951 SC 332
J. Mohapatra & Co. v. State of Orissa, (1984) 4 SCC 103
Union of India v. G. Ganayutham, (1997) 7 SCC 463

explanation: The rule that no one may be a judge in their own cause gives way where no other body can act. This is the doctrine of necessity, and the case is J. Mohapatra & Co. v State of Orissa.

explanation: Statement 1 is correct: a certificate may be suspended on the subscriber's request or in the public interest. Statement 2 is false: a suspension cannot continue indefinitely without giving the subscriber a chance to be heard.

stem: According to the Indian Contract Act, 1872, when is the communication of an acceptance complete against the proposer?

options.text: When the acceptor prepares the letter of acceptance
When it is dispatched beyond the control of the acceptor
When it is delivered to the office of the proposer party
When the proposer acknowledges receipt in his records

explanation: As against the proposer, the communication of an acceptance is complete when it is put in the course of transmission so that it is out of the acceptor's power to withdraw it.

stem: After a government notification is issued for acquiring farmland under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the owner notices decreasing income from crops until possession is taken. What type of loss is compensable?

options.text: Loss due to falling land prices in the market
Loss due to cancellation of tenant agreements
Loss of employment in nearby areas
Bona fide diminution of profits due to acquisition process

explanation: Compensation on acquisition covers loss that flows from the acquisition process, such as genuine diminution of profits between the notification and taking possession. Falling market prices, cancelled tenancies and loss of jobs nearby are not compensable heads.

stem:
Under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, when an offence is committed by a company, every person in charge and responsible at the time is deemed guilty, unless he proves lack of knowledge or due diligence.
Conclusions:
I. A company as well as its responsible officers may be held liable for environmental offences under the Act.
II. An officer of a company can never escape liability once the company is found guilty of an offence. Which one of the following is correct?

options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

explanation: Conclusion I follows: the Act makes both the company and the persons in charge liable. Conclusion II does not follow, because the statement itself allows an officer to escape liability by proving lack of knowledge or due diligence; "can never escape" contradicts that.

stem:

explanation: Under the Negotiable Instruments Act a negotiable instrument given without consideration creates no obligation of payment between the parties, and where the consideration fails only in part, the holder in immediate relation recovers in proportion. Both statements are correct.

stem:
Given below are two statements — Assertion (A) and Reason (R):

Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

explanation: A person interested in a forfeited newspaper may apply to the High Court within two months. The reason is false because the Special Bench is not always of exactly three judges. So the assertion is true and the reason is false.

stem: Under which provision can a citizen file a public case in the Court of Magistrate regarding issues of public interest?

Section 144 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
Section 133 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

explanation: The provision allowing a Magistrate to deal with a public nuisance on a complaint or information is the one on conditional orders for removal of nuisance.

stem: How long does the registered address furnished under Section 14A(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, remain valid if not changed?

options.text: Six years after final determination of the cause
Three years after the institution of the suit
Two years after final determination of the cause
Five years from the date of decree

explanation: The question concerns how long an address given under the cited section stays valid. The key says six years after the final determination of the cause.

stem: According to the Copyright Act, 1957, what is ordinarily the maximum punishment for copyright infringement under Section 63?

options.text: Imprisonment up to three years and fine up to two lakh rupees
Imprisonment up to two years and fine up to one lakh rupees
Imprisonment up to five years and fine up to five lakh rupees
Imprisonment up to seven years and fine up to five lakh rupees

explanation: The Copyright Act punishes infringement with imprisonment of at least six months and up to three years and a fine of fifty thousand to two lakh rupees.

stem: Which condition must be satisfied for things said or done by one conspirator to be admissible against another under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?

options.text: The statement must be made after the conspiracy has ended
The statement must involve unrelated matters of personal benefit
There must be reasonable ground to believe a conspiracy exists
There must be proof that each conspirator personally committed the act

explanation: The acts and statements of one conspirator can be used against another only where there is reasonable ground to believe that the persons conspired together.

stem: According to Section 25(a) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, what happens if the claimant fails to submit his statement of claim without sufficient cause?

options.text: The tribunal adjourns the case indefinitely
The tribunal imposes a penalty but continues proceedings
The tribunal assumes the claim is admitted

explanation: If the claimant fails to file his statement of claim without sufficient cause, the arbitral tribunal terminates the proceedings.

stem: Under Section 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, what is the maximum period of detention in civil prison for a decree amount exceeding 5,000?
explanation: The Code limits detention in civil prison by the amount of the decree: up to six weeks where the decree is above 2,000 but not above 5,000 rupees, and up to three months where it exceeds 5,000.

stem: If a person attempts an offence punishable with a maximum of 10 years imprisonment, what is the maximum years of imprisonment that can be imposed under Section 62 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: An attempt to commit an offence is punishable with up to half the longest term of imprisonment for the offence. For an offence with a maximum of ten years that is five years.

stem:
Assertion (A): An employee can be deemed to be in continuous service for one year only if he has worked for 365 days in the preceding twelve months without any interruption.
Reason (R): Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, continuous service may also include periods of interruption due to sickness, accident, leave, lay-off, strike, or lock-out not caused by the employee’s fault.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

explanation: Continuous service under the Gratuity Act does not require 365 days without any break; the Act counts service as continuous even through certain interruptions and uses a lower number of working days for the one-year test. The assertion is therefore false, and the reason correctly states the Act's approach.

stem: According to the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, what is the fixed amount of compensation payable in the event of death caused by a motor vehicle accident under no-fault liability?
explanation: The Motor Vehicles Act pays a fixed sum without proof of fault for death in an accident. The amount has been raised by amendment over the years, and the figure in the key (one lakh rupees) does not match the amounts I know from the Act.

Punishable under Section 66 of the IT Act, 2000 + compensation claimable
Customers have no legal remedy under IT Act

explanation: Hacking a computer system and stealing data is an offence under the Act's provisions on computer-related offences, and the Act also lets those who suffer loss claim compensation, so both remedies are available.

stem: Mr. Rajesh issued a cheque of 50,000 to his supplier, Mr. Sharma, for the payment of goods purchased. When Mr. Sharma deposited the cheque, it was returned by the bank with the remark ”Insufficient Funds.” On the basis of the above problem, select the correct option.

A complaint in writing is to be made by Mr. Sharma in the court within one month for the dishonour of the cheque.
A complaint in writing is to be made by Mr. Sharma in the court within five months for the dishonour of the cheque.
A complaint in writing is to be made by Mr. Sharma in the court within two months for the dishonour of the cheque.

explanation: When a cheque is returned for insufficient funds, the payee must give the drawer a written demand within the time the Negotiable Instruments Act allows, and complain to the court within one month after the notice period ends without payment. The answer is one month.

stem: ”A”, a real estate developer, entered into a contract with ”B”, the owner of a piece of land, for the purchase of her property. However, after receiving the advance payment, ”B” refused to execute the sale deed claiming that she received a better offer from another buyer. ”A” demanded the enforcement of the contract under the Specific Relief Act, 1963, but ”B” denied his claim. ”A” has to file a suit in a court of law.

options.text: ”A” may file a suit in the criminal court having the powers under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
”A” may file a suit in the special court constituted under the Specific Relief Act, 1963.
”A” may file a suit in the civil court having powers under the Civil Procedure Code, 1908.
No suit can be brought against ”A” as there is no breach of contract.

explanation: Where the owner of land refuses to execute the sale deed after taking the advance, the buyer can sue in a civil court for specific performance or damages; criminal courts and special courts are not the forum.

stem: Read the statements: 1. Agricultural income is exempt from tax under Section 10(1) of Income Tax Act, 1961. 2. Non-agricultural income above exemption + agricultural income above 5000 is taxable via partial integration.
explanation: Agricultural income is exempt from tax. When a person also has non-agricultural income above the exemption limit and agricultural income above the stated limit, the rate of tax is worked out by partial integration. Both statements describe this correctly.

stem: Mr K is owner of a building containing many rooms and earns rent from it. Mr Y is owner of an adjacent cotton mill which causes noise and smoke, forcing tenants to vacate rooms and resulting in loss of rent for Mr K. Which tort applies?
explanation: Noise and smoke from a neighbouring mill that make the plaintiff's property unfit for use interfere with the enjoyment of land, which is nuisance.

stem: Mr B told Mr A to leave the premises in occupation of Mr A. When Mr A refused, Mr B collected some of his workmen who mustered round Mr A. They tucked up their sleeves and aprons and threatened to break the plaintiff’s neck, but did not leave. Under which tortious act, Mr A can file the case?
explanation: Workmen who gathered round the plaintiff, tucked up their sleeves and threatened to break his neck put him in fear of immediate violence without touching him. That is assault.

stem: Ms J, a banker refuses to honour a cheque of Ms F despite sufficient balance. Ms F suffers no monetary loss. Which maxim applies?
explanation: A bank that wrongly refuses to honour a cheque violates the customer's legal right even if no money is lost. That is a legal wrong without actual damage (injuria sine damno).

stem:

(1) Cyber Cafes
(2) Telecom Regulators
(3) Social Media Platforms
(4) Internet Service Providers
explanation: An intermediary under the Act includes service providers such as internet service providers, online platforms and cyber cafes that handle electronic records for others. A telecom regulator is a regulator, not a service provider, so it is not included.

stem: Advocate Mr. X was representing a client, Mr. Y, in a property dispute case. It is only an offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 2018
It amounts to criminal conspiracy under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
It amounts to the Contempt of Court under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971

explanation: Taking a bribe to delay a client's case is professional misconduct under the Bar Council's rules, and may in addition be an offence under other laws. The statement that it violates the Bar Council rules is correct.

stem: Under Section 15 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 the divorced person, to marry again:

options.text: Has to wait for one year from the date of decree
Has to wait for six months from the date of decree
May marry immediately thereafter without leave of court

explanation: Once a decree of divorce has been passed and the time to appeal has expired or the appeal is dismissed, either party may marry again; the Act no longer requires a waiting period or the court's leave.

stem: Which of the following is not an advantage of ADR?
explanation: Alternative dispute resolution is usually faster, cheaper and more confidential than litigation, but it does not always end in a binding decision, as mediation and conciliation produce binding results only on settlement.

stem: Under Section 146 of the BSA 2023, when are leading questions permissible in court proceedings?

options.text: Always allowed in examination-in-chief without restriction
Can be asked in any stage without objection
Permitted during cross-examination and when matters are introductory, undisputed, or proved

explanation: Leading questions are not allowed in examination-in-chief or re-examination, except on introductory or undisputed matters, but are allowed in cross-examination.

stem: A manufacturing company in Surat named “X” has been discharging untreated industrial waste into a nearby river, violating the Environment Protection Act, 1986 and the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974. Based on the above problem, select the correct answer.

options.text: It is the violation of Section 24 of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.
It is the violation of Section 40 of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.
It is not the violation of the provisions of the laws stated in the problem.
It is the violation of Section 23 of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.

explanation: Discharging untreated industrial waste into a stream is prohibited by the section of the Water Act that bars putting polluting matter into streams, wells or sewers, so the company violates that section.

stem: In 2020 at Dhorodo village the Panchayat elections could not happen due to Covid pandemic while the tenure of the Panchayat was getting over that year itself. Mr. Haribansh represented the people that year at the Panchayat post dissolution of the Panchayat tenure and made a law exercising the delegated power, vide, the Panchayati Raj Act of the state to restrict economic activities per day to 100 only. In which of the following cases this is allowed or restricted?

options.text: Jalan Trading vs. Union of India

explanation: The question is about a delegated power exercised by a panchayat office-holder and tests a case on delegation; the key names the case on delegated legislation among those listed.

stem:

Reason (R): PIL allows any public-spirited person to approach the court on behalf of those who cannot represent themselves.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

explanation: Standing is relaxed in PIL so that any public-spirited person can approach the court for those who cannot do so themselves. The reason correctly explains the assertion.

stem: 1980s bonded labour case – what did SC hold?

options.text: Right to free legal aid is only directive, not fundamental
Monetary relief only, no systemic reforms
Right against forced labour is fundamental right under Art. 21
Only govt. agencies can file labour petitions

explanation: In the bonded labour case the Supreme Court held that the right against forced labour is part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21.

stem: Kiran wins arbitral award; Meera refuses to pay citing irregularities. Kiran seeks court enforcement. Which ACA 1996 section applies?

options.text: Section 36 – automatic enforcement unless set aside

explanation: An arbitral award is enforceable like a court decree once the time to challenge it has passed or the challenge has failed; the pendency of a challenge does not by itself stop enforcement. This is the section on enforcement.

stem: Where a document is executed in several parts like printing, lithography or photography, video recording, computer resource as electronic or digital records, the BSA 2023 classifies each part as:
explanation: When a document is executed in several parts, each part is primary evidence of the document, and electronic or digital records can be primary evidence as well.

stem: In a criminal trial, Rajesh is accused of theft. During investigation, the police recover a stolen laptop from a location frequented by Rajesh. His fingerprints are found on the laptop. According to the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, how should the court interpret this evidence?

options.text: The recovered laptop and fingerprints are automatically considered conclusive proof of Rajesh’s guilt.
The recovered laptop and fingerprints are circumstantial evidence that can be considered along with other evidence, but do not by themselves prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
The evidence is inadmissible because the police did not obtain a search warrant.
The fingerprints must be verified by at least two independent forensic experts before being presented in court.

explanation: Recovery of the stolen item from a place the accused frequents, with his fingerprints on it, is circumstantial evidence. It can be considered with the rest of the evidence but does not by itself prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

stem: Existence of course of business when relevant is discussed in:
explanation: Whether something was done in the ordinary course of business is a relevant fact. In the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 this is Section 14.

stem: A suit is pending in District Court A, but one of the parties, Meera, requests its transfer to District Court B, claiming bias of the judge. The opposing party objects, stating the request is baseless. Who has the authority to decide whether the suit can be transferred?

options.text: The District Court A where the suit is pending
The High Court or the Supreme Court
The Civil Judge in District Court B

explanation: A party can ask a higher court to transfer a suit to another court. That power belongs to the High Court or the Supreme Court, not the court where the suit is pending or the court it is asked to move to.

stem: What is the minimum percentage of affected families that need to give their prior consent for acquiring land for private companies as per the Right To Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013?
explanation: For acquisition for private companies the Act requires the prior consent of at least eighty per cent of affected families.

stem: Which of the following is the time limit given under Section 17 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882?

options.text: A period of 18 years from the date of transfer.

explanation: The section on accumulation of income limits the period to the life of the transferor or eighteen years from the transfer, whichever is longer. Option C refers to the life of the transferee, which does not match.

stem: Maya files a suit in Court A for the recovery of money from Neha. During proceedings, Neha requests that Seema be added as a defendant, claiming Seema is liable. Maya objects. The Court reviews the application and decides Seema should be included as a defendant. Which principle of CPC is applied?

options.text: Order 1, Rule 10 – Joinder and Substitution of Parties

explanation: A request to add a person as a defendant is dealt with under the order on joinder and substitution of parties, not under rules on rejection of plaints, service of summons or amendment of pleadings.

stem:
Consider the following statements and answer: Mr. Patel, being a police officer, receives a complaint that Raju was involved in a robbery of bank property and helped to hide valuables in his farm, as stated by villagers. With this regard:
(1) The Police Officer Mr. Patel may arrest Raju without warrant when Raju can be arrested only if he commits a non-cognizable offence in the presence of Mr. Patel.
(2) Since the reasonable complaint against Raju has been received and strong suspicion exists, he can be immediately arrested.
(3) Raju can be arrested only when he tries to escape or run away.
(4) Raju can be arrested to prevent him from making inducement, threat, or promise to wit- nesses.
explanation: A police officer may arrest without a warrant where a reasonable complaint or credible information shows that a person has committed a cognizable offence, and also to prevent a person tampering with witnesses. Statements (2) and (4) are of these kinds; (1) and (3) are not.

stem: Which of the following injunction can be granted only by the decree made at hearing and upon the merit of the suit?
explanation: A temporary injunction can be granted at any stage and lasts until further order. A perpetual injunction is granted only by a decree after hearing the case on its merits.

stem: Which of the following would be the first previous year in case of a business or profession newly set up on 31st March, 2020 as per the Income Tax Act, 1961?

options.text: Start from 1st April, 2019 and will end on 31st March, 2020.
Start from 31st March, 2020 and will end on 31st March, 2020.
Start from 1st April, 2020 and will end on 31st December, 2020.
Start from 1st January, 2020 and will end on 31st March, 2020.

explanation: For a business newly set up, the first previous year begins on the date of setting up and ends on the following 31 March. Here both fall on 31 March 2020.

stem: The Gloucester Grammar School case relates to which of the following important maxims?
explanation: In the Gloucester Grammar School case a new school took away pupils from an older school and no legal right was violated; the loss was damage without legal injury, which is the maxim damnum sine injuria.

stem: Which of the following is incorrect with respect to arbitration agreement as per the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996?

options.text: Arbitration agreement may be written as well as oral.
Arbitration agreement may be in the form of a separate agreement.
Arbitration agreement may be in the form of an arbitration clause in a contract.
Arbitration agreement may be for all or certain disputes which may arise between the parties.

explanation: An arbitration agreement must be in writing; an oral agreement is not enough. The statement that it may be oral is therefore the incorrect one.

stem: Amit, intending to cause the death of Vijay, attacks him with a knife. Vijay sustains severe injuries and dies on the spot. The investigation reveals that Amit acted with knowledge that his actions were likely to cause death. However, there is no evidence of premeditation or intent to murder Vijay. Which of the following offences has Amit committed?

options.text: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 of IPC
Causing death by negligence under Section 304A of IPC
Voluntarily causing grievous hurt under Section 325 of IPC

explanation: The facts say the accused intended to cause death and death resulted. Intentional killing is ordinarily murder unless an exception applies; culpable homicide not amounting to murder applies where an exception such as grave provocation fits or the intent was less than a death-causing one.

stem:
The Parliament enacts the “Fair Housing Act, 2024,” which includes the following provisions: (1) Section 3: Prohibits discrimination in renting or selling houses based on religion, caste, or gender.

(3) Section 10: Makes it mandatory for landlords to disclose the religious background of all tenants in the previous 10 years. The Supreme Court declares Section 10 unconstitutional but upholds the other provisions of the law. What principle did the court apply in this decision?
explanation: When a court strikes down one provision of an Act as unconstitutional but upholds the rest because the rest can stand on its own, it applies the doctrine of severability.

stem: In which of the following case an electronic record shall not be attributed to the originator as per the Information Technology Act, 2000?

options.text: Electronic record sent by the originator himself.
Electronic record sent by an authorised person.
Electronic record sent by an automated system programmed by him.
Electronic record sent by an unauthorized person.

explanation: An electronic record is attributed to the originator if he sent it, if a person authorised to act for him sent it, or if an information system programmed by him sent it. A record sent by an unauthorised person is not attributed to him.

stem: Who among the following is not included in the definition of a workman as per the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947?

A supervisor drawing monthly salary of |8,000.
A supervisor drawing monthly salary of |10,000.
A supervisor drawing monthly salary of |12,000.

explanation: A supervisor is within the definition of workman only if his monthly wages do not exceed the ceiling in the definition. The highest salary listed is above that ceiling, so that supervisor is not a workman.

stem: Which of the following is generally not considered as a valid condition for a Hindu marriage as per the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955?

options.text: The parties should not have a spouse living at the time of the marriage.
The parties should be within the degrees of prohibited relationship.
The parties should not be sapindas of each other.
The parties should not be suffering from epilepsy.

explanation: The statutory conditions for a Hindu marriage concern monogamy, mental capacity, age, prohibited relationship and sapinda relationship. Epilepsy is not a ground in the conditions as now worded.

stem: In which of the following circumstances an arbitrator may not be challenged as per the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996?

options.text: When a justifiable doubt as to his independence arises.
When a justifiable doubt as to his impartiality arises.
When he possesses the qualifications agreed by the party.
When he becomes ineligible as per the seventh schedule of the Act.

explanation: An arbitrator can be challenged for justifiable doubts about independence or impartiality or for ineligibility, but not simply because he has the qualifications the parties agreed.

stem: A is accused of the murder of B by beating him. Which of the following will not be considered as relevant fact forming part of the same transaction as per the Indian Evidence Act, 1872?

options.text: Whatever said by A or B at the time of beating.
Whatever done by A or B at the time of beating.
Whatever said by by-standers at the time of beating.
Whatever said by A or B a day before the day of beating.

explanation: Acts and statements that are part of the same transaction are relevant when they occur at the time of the event. Something said a day before is separated in time and is not part of the same transaction.

stem: Which of the following cannot be considered as the suit of civil nature for Section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908?

options.text: Suit for recovery of voluntary payments or offerings.
Suit relating to rights of worship.

explanation: A suit is of a civil nature when it concerns a civil right, even if religious questions are involved. Suits about franchise, specific relief and the right of worship concern civil rights; a suit to recover voluntary offerings does not, because no legal right to them exists.

stem: Which of the following offences may be tried summarily as per the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973?

options.text: Offence under Section 454 of the IPC.
Offence under Section 504 of the IPC.
Offence punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years.

explanation: Offences punishable with imprisonment of up to two years, and certain listed offences, may be tried summarily. Offences punishable with life imprisonment cannot.

stem: Which of the following is incorrect statement in the light of Indian Evidence Act, 1872?

options.text: Confession always goes against a person making it.
Admissions are conclusive as to the matters admitted.
Admissions may operate as an estoppel.
Confession is a statement, written or oral, which is a direct admission of guilt.

explanation: Admissions are not conclusive proof of what they admit; they can be explained or rebutted, although they may operate as estoppels. The statement that admissions are conclusive is therefore the incorrect one.

stem: Which of the following is correct according to the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 pertaining to proof of contents of the documents?

options.text: Contents of the documents shall be proved by primary evidence.
Contents of the documents may be proved by secondary evidence.
Contents of the documents shall be proved by both primary and secondary evidence.
Contents of documents may be proved either by primary or by secondary evidence.

explanation: The contents of a document may be proved either by primary evidence (the document itself) or, in the cases the Act allows, by secondary evidence. The options that say only one kind "shall" be used are too rigid.

stem: In which of the following situation plaintiff is precluded from bringing a fresh suit as per the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908?

options.text: Dismissal of suit where summons not served in consequence of plaintiff’s failure to pay costs.
Dismissal of suit because neither party appeared.
Dismissal of suit because plaintiff did not appear.
Dismissal of suit because plaintiff did not apply for fresh summons within given time limit once it returned unserved.

explanation: When a suit is dismissed because the plaintiff does not appear, the order is one on the plaintiff's default and a fresh suit on the same cause of action is barred under the rule on dismissal for default; the other situations leave the plaintiff free to sue again.

stem: Which of the following provision of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 makes the doctrine of res judicata applicable in representative suits?
explanation: The res judicata rule is extended to representative suits by one of the explanations to the section on res judicata; the one dealing with persons litigating on behalf of others in a public or common interest is the sixth.

stem: Under which of the following situation wife is not entitled for maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973?

options.text: Husband presumes that wife is living in adultery.
Voluntarily wife refuses to live with husband.
Wife living separately as husband keeps a mistress.
Wife is forcefully removed from the house.

explanation: A wife is denied maintenance if she lives in adultery, refuses without sufficient reason to live with her husband, or lives apart by mutual consent. Voluntary refusal to live with the husband is the one listed here; the other situations give her a good reason or no fault.

stem: In which of the following situations right of private defence can not extend to causing death?

options.text: In case when an assault is causing apprehension of murder.
In case when assault is reflecting intention of committing rape.
In case when assault is reflecting intention of causing simple hurt.
In case when assault is reflecting intention of gratifying unnatural lust.

explanation: The right of private defence of the body extends to causing death only in the serious situations the Code lists, such as apprehension of death, grievous hurt or rape. An assault meant only to cause simple hurt does not justify causing death.

stem:
In which of the following situations Indian Penal Code, 1860 may not apply?
i. An offence committed by Indians outside India.
ii. An offence committed by any person on any ship registered in India.
iii. Any person committing offence targeting computer resources located in any country.
explanation: The Penal Code applies to offences by Indians outside India, to offences on ships or aircraft registered in India, and to offences targeting computers located in India. Statement iii refers to computer resources in any country, which goes beyond that reach, so it is the situation where the Code may not apply.
